exit_criterion: PROPOSAL.md section 16: "A complete calibration workflow on a real NIR dataset matches reference software within stated tolerance." Concretely, and demonstrated rather than reasoned: a real NIR dataset is imported, preprocessed, split, fitted with PLS, cross-validated and read back - the metrics, the predicted-versus-actual plot and the residuals - without leaving the application, and the numbers agree with the parity programme's reference within the tolerances docs/parity-report.md publishes. The phase ends when that run is recorded with its evidence, not when every entry below is passing. Section 16 also names PLS regression and PLS-DA, the full validation suite, Hotelling T2, SPE, VIP and contribution plots, predicted-versus-actual and residual plots, a train/test splitting UI, and the Bruker OPUS reader. Of those only PLS has a kernel (#88 is the executor half); the rest have no entry on this list yet, and the list is not complete until they do.

features.title: A node under a range selection can be plotted
features.user_visible_behavior: Selecting a wavelength range no longer empties the spectra plot for the rest of the branch. Every node downstream of a range_select draws against the axis it actually has.
verification: GET /api/spectra/{node} returns a payload for a node under a range_select, with axis.values matching the selection rather than the dataset.
GET /api/results/{node} under a range selection returns loadings.axis the same length as its components.
The axis is correct for two chained range selections, and for a sibling branch that has none.
uv run pytest - the existing suite, plus a case asserting the axis a selected node reports.
features.evidence: 2026-09-05. Against the live mango project over HTTP, after the fix: GET /api/spectra/{node} returns an aligned payload for every node under the 500-1000 nm selection - vis_nir, snv, snv_d1 and d2 each 167 axis values [501-999 nm] against 167 trace points, while source and full_centre stay 306 [285-1200 nm]. Every one of the four was a 500 before. GET /api/results/{node}: pca_snv and pca_d2 now publish 167 axis values [501-999 nm] beside 167 loadings, where they published 306 [285-1200 nm] beside 167 with no error; pca_full is unchanged at 306/306. uv run pytest - 787 passed, 1 skipped (775 before, +12 in tests/test_node_axis.py: the source axis, a selection, inheritance down the chain, two selections composing, a sibling branch unaffected, a descending wavenumber axis, both payloads, and both refusals). uv run ruff check, ruff format --check (76 files) and mypy (52 source files) exit 0. Frontend: npx tsc -b --noEmit and npx vitest run - 10 files, 77 tests passed, unchanged, because the payload shape did not move.
features.notes: Found running the application end to end against the mango dry-matter set (Anderson et al. 2020, 285-1200 nm, 7413 x 306), whose first necessary step is a range selection because 285-500 nm and 1191-1200 nm are zero-padded dark channels. The axis is computed and discarded, not unknown: RangeSelectTransformer.selected_axis() exists at preprocessing.py:478, the executor deliberately keeps no per-node axis (executor.py:5-8), and spectra_payload reads only version.axis.values (api.py:588) before raising at api.py:595. The fix that keeps the executor's guarantees is to fold the range_select masks down the node's ancestry in the HTTP layer - a pure function of the recipe, so no new cached state and no content hash moves. Carrying an axis beside each node's array in the executor is the other option and the larger one. Found on picking it up: results/{node} has the same cause and does not raise - results_payload builds loadings.axis from version.axis unconditionally (api.py:443-450), so pca_snv under a 500-1000 nm selection served 167 loadings against a 306-value axis with no error. One bug, two symptoms; the fix belongs at the shared question of what axis a node is on, not in either payload. Fixed by node_axis(pipeline, node_id, version) in api.py, which folds the range_select steps down the node's ancestry - a pure function of the recipe, so it reads no array and cannot move a content hash or invalidate a cache entry, which is what let the executor keep its no-per-node-axis guarantee. The mask comes from RangeSelectTransformer rather than being restated, so the interval's meaning is stated once. Both payloads take an optional axis and both now check it: the spectra 500 stays for a width no step accounts for, and results_payload gained the same check, because serving a mismatch silently is worse than refusing. Impact measured on the way past: frontend/src/plot/analysis.ts:55 plots loadings.axis.values as x against components as y, and Plotly truncates to the shorter array, so 167 loadings were being drawn against 285-783 nm instead of 501-999 nm - every peak displaced by about 216 nm.

features.title: Each model-to-row mapping is written once, not twice
features.user_visible_behavior: Nothing changes for the user. A column added to the schema reaches both the normal path and the import that reads a pre-database directory, because there is one place to add it.
verification: uv run pytest - unchanged in count and content, the import path's tests included.
cd frontend && npx playwright test - 38 passed.
features.evidence: 2026-08-30. `uv run pytest` - 758 passed, 1 skipped, the same suite as before the change. `cd frontend && npx playwright test` - 38 passed. ruff, format and mypy clean over 49 files. project.py is 38 lines shorter and the seven remaining db.*Row( constructions are the seven builders. Merged as #132.
features.notes: Cleanup found at the Phase 1.3 checkpoint, filed as #131 rather than folded into a feature branch. Six mappings were stated twice - once on the normal path, once in _import_json_project - and the copy that would be forgotten when a column is added is the import path, which has one test and no user until someone opens an old project. Two smaller things went with it: a test asserting datasets.json does not exist, which could no longer fail because nothing writes that file; and the server's lifespan leaving every SQLite engine holding its file, which costs nothing on process exit and is what locks a file on Windows. An unused-export scan flagged fourteen names - executor.NodeOutput, checks.PipelineWarning, project.PROJECT_FILE among them - and none was deleted: each is used inside its own module or is the type a caller receives, so removing them would be churn dressed as cleanup.

features.title: A branch is dragged on the canvas, and a node can be removed
features.user_visible_behavior: Dragging from a node's output port to another node's input port points that node at a new parent, and a control on the node removes it, reconnecting its children to its parent. A connection that would make a cycle does not drop, and says why.
verification: cd frontend && npx vitest run - the graph rules in edits.ts, including every refusal.
cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/pipeline.spec.ts - the drag and the removal in a browser.
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. `npx vitest run` - 10 files, 77 tests passed, including src/__tests__/edits.test.ts (14 tests: connect replaces the target's input, a fork gives one node two children, cycle/self/source-target/duplicate/unknown are refused, removal reconnects every child, the source is refused). `npx playwright test` - 38 passed across all four projects, including the four new cases in e2e/pipeline.spec.ts: msc->centre_a rewires and the edge count stays 13, pca_a->snv is refused with 'would make a cycle' and no edge appears, removing snv leaves source->centre_a and source->snv_savgol with 13 nodes, and the source node carries no remove control. `npx tsc -b --noEmit` and `npx eslint .` both exit 0.
features.notes: Items 1 and 4 of #51. The rules live in frontend/src/canvas/edits.ts, pure and tested, and are enforced during the drag through React Flow's isValidConnection - each refusal is the client half of a models.py validator. Every non-source node holds exactly one input (tuple[NodeId]), so connecting replaces rather than appends and a branch is one node with several children; an edge cannot be cut on its own because the child would be left dangling. The remove control is on the node rather than in the side panel: clicking a node opens its tab, which replaces the panel before it could be used. Edits are held locally and saved by the existing whole-list PUT (#108). Node positions are still not draggable - layout lives in pipeline_state.json and nothing writes it back.

features.title: A pipeline says which estimator nodes will not be fitted
features.user_visible_behavior: A pipeline holding a PLS or PLS-DA node is told so before it is run, rather than reporting a successful run with a node that silently never fitted.
verification: POST /api/pipelines/{id}/validate returns a warning naming every PLS and PLS-DA node; a pipeline without one still returns warnings: [].
A run over such a pipeline still succeeds - what is said changes, what is executed does not.
uv run pytest
features.evidence: 2026-09-05. Against the live mango pipeline, which holds a PLS node on a mean-centred branch: POST /api/pipelines/current/validate returned valid: false with one warning - code 'estimator_not_fitted', node_id 'pls_dm', severity 'info', and the sentence "'pls' at 'pls_dm' has no kernel in this build and will not be fitted. The run will report success and this node will stay unrun; every other node is unaffected." It returned valid: true, problems: [], warnings: [] before. Node states are unchanged: 11 of 12 complete, pls_dm not_run. uv run pytest - 793 passed, 1 skipped (787 before, +6 in tests/test_not_fitted_warning.py). uv run ruff check, ruff format --check (77 files) and mypy (53 source files) exit 0. Frontend npx tsc -b --noEmit and npx vitest run - 10 files, 77 tests passed, unchanged.
features.notes: Not #88, which is the kernel. This is the silence around it, found end to end: validate returned valid: true with no warnings, the job reported succeeded and 'Done', and the PLS node was left 'not_run' - the same state a node has before it has ever been run, so a screen cannot tell 'not yet' from 'never will be'. Run.pending_estimators (executor.py:279, populated at :432) already names the declined nodes and the string 'pending_estimators' appears nowhere in api.py. The warnings list is already in the validate payload and already rendered. This should become redundant when #88 lands. Built in api.py's validation_payload rather than in checks.py, deliberately: that module's docstring states its contract - every warning there catches a mistake whose symptom is a plausible result, with a document behind it - and this is neither. Nothing is wrong with the recipe; the build is short a kernel. Filing it under 'what is wrong with your pipeline' would blame the user for #88. Two sources, one list, told apart by code and severity ('info' rather than 'warning'). executor.has_kernel(spec) is now the one place that knows what can be fitted, asked by the executor's routing and by the warning, so #88 adds to one tuple rather than editing two files. The state half of the issue - pipelines/{id}/state telling 'not yet' from 'never will be' - was left: frontend NodeState is a closed union in canvas/graph.ts:12, so it needs a type change, a NodeCard switch case and a visual treatment with no artboard behind it, and #88 makes it moot. PipelineCanvas.tsx:190 already renders problems.join(' . ') when valid is false, so the sentence reaches the canvas with no frontend change and nothing blocks the run.

features.notes: Found end to end on the mango set, whose CSV is 'sample_id, 285.0, ..., 1200.0, target_DM': the import recorded targets {sample_id, target_DM} and sample_ids [] for 7413 samples, so sample_id is selectable as a PLS response and every trace falls back to 'row N'. This is readers/delimited.py:34-35 doing exactly what it documents, so the rule is what needs deciding, not the code. The sharper half is that /import/preview reports head.sample_ids ['1','2',...] for the same file the import keeps none for - two answers to one question. corrections is an object of strings covering delimiter, decimal and orientation only (api.py:333), so a user who sees the wrong role in the preview cannot overrule it, which is the one guess the reader does not offer a Choice for. Needs a decision before a branch: detect better, add column role to the Choice set, or both.
